correctness.rationale: For each n>=4 every four-vertex induced subgraph is connected exactly when kappa>=n-3. Complementing sends 1+3 and 2+2 disconnections to forbidden K1,3 and K2,2 subgraphs. Max degree at most two and absence of induced cycles >=5 in permutation graphs imply disjoint paths and triangles. Value complementation and unique direct-sum decomposition, with exact path block multiplicities, prove the rational weighted series. Matchings give Fibonacci cumulative n-2 connectivity; the complete graph is unique at n-1. The standalone verifier reproduces full permutation counts, exact connectivity through n=7, four-set threshold at n=8, and all q coefficients. Finite checks are not substituted for the general proof.

The scalar a_n sequence and recurrence are already OEIS A180965 and are explicitly excluded from novelty claims; published path-permutation counts are used as existing ingredients. residual_risks: The numerical sequence is already OEIS A180965; claiming novelty for that unweighted sequence alone would be false.

Semantic retrieval is not a proof of exhaustive historical priority.

value.rationale: The motivating source explicitly asks for understanding the distribution of inversion-graph vertex connectivity but gives only seven rows. The theorem completely characterizes its three extremal high-connectivity layers for all n and refines the tail by original noninversions. Identifying a high-connectivity family with path–triangle sum classes is structural information not supplied by the known unweighted tatami sequence and provides a tractable entry to the otherwise unknown full distribution.
